core_obligations: Reduce to finding one suitable closed point in every nonempty open, and choose an etale morphism from an open subscheme U of X onto an open of affine space (proof lines 4669-4678).
Use openness of the etale morphism and the affine space lemma to find a closed point w in its image whose residue field is finite separable over k, and pick a preimage x (proof lines 4679-4684).

Conclude that kappa(x)/kappa(w) is finite separable by the etale structure over a field, hence kappa(x)/k is finite separable, and that x is closed in X because its residue field is algebraic over k (proof lines 4684-4690).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to one point per nonempty open and choose an etale chart (proof lines 4669-4678).
Find a suitable point downstairs (proof lines 4679-4684).
Lift it and check closedness (proof lines 4684-4690).
difficulty_reason: If X is smooth over the spectrum of a field k, the lemma shows that the closed points whose residue field is a finite separable extension of k form a dense subset (statement lines 4657-4666). It suffices to find one such point in every nonempty open, so the proof chooses a diagram in which X receives an etale morphism from an open subscheme of an affine space; etaleness makes that morphism open, and the affine space case supplies a closed point with finite separable residue field inside its image (proof lines 4668-4684). Lifting that point along the etale morphism preserves finite separability of the residue field extension by the structure of etale morphisms over a field, and the lifted point is closed in X because algebraic residue field extensions characterize closed points (proof lines 4684-4690). The claim is H2: three standard inputs arranged so that the problem is transferred to affine space and back, with no step referred to the reader.
